decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already adds the addressable LEDs to 3.3V measurement coverage, while 5V monitoring remains required for the 5V sensors.
The standalone regulator already powers the full shared 3.3V rail; moving the LEDs onto that rail does not invalidate or necessarily change any recorded attribute.
The LED supply change does not alter the sensor-board connector inventory, sensor interfaces, or documented sensor supply connections.
The AXP2101 power-path topology and DCDC1 output remain valid; the source changes a downstream LED load rather than the power path itself.
The requirement to cut LED standby power separately from sensor power remains unchanged, and its current state contains no obsolete 5V-specific switching attribute.
Moving the LEDs to 3.3V does not change the established 3.4V DCDC1 configuration or the requirement to maintain the system rail at 3.3V.
The interboard connectors still carry both 3.3V and 5V, and the source does not change any connector, pinout, or board-distribution topology.
The LED supply and level-shifter decision does not affect the panel-mounted PWRON button connector or its control behavior.
The source decision does not affect the battery connector type, mounting, pin count, or unresolved pinout.
The existing same-message MODIFY fully records the 3.3V LED supply, direct ESP32 data drive, removal of the level-shifter part, and accepted indicator-brightness condition.
The LED power change does not affect the SPS30 SEL pin connection or its I2C mode.
The client explicitly eliminates the LED level shifter, so the previously required level-shifter part is obsolete in the assembly-ready BOM.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The LEDs are now powered from 3.3V instead of 5V. At 3.3V supply the SK6812 data threshold drops to 2.31V, which the ESP32 3.3V output satisfies directly, so no level shifter is needed. The tradeoff is that 3.3V is slightly below the SK6812 datasheet minimum (3.7V), but it works reliably at indicator brightness levels.
